rubrics.justification: Accurately identifies a good-quality blastocyst with compact ICM and less cohesive TE, and appropriately notes possible expansion-stage ambiguity; minor limitation is some image-based speculation (collapse/debris) from a single static view.
Thoroughly integrates age, prior live birth, tubal factor, sperm quality, endometrium, BMI, AMH, and lifestyle factors with embryo quality and prognosis, including the important hydrosalpinx caveat.

Reasoning is logical and well structured, with conclusions generally supported by morphology and clinical context; slight overreach in assigning precise prognostic impact to TE and in discussing 3AB vs 4AB inconsistency without full image certainty.

Recommendations are largely consistent with Gardner grading, single embryo transfer in a young good-prognosis patient, and standard IVF practice; minor caveat is that some probability framing and PGT-A discussion are more practice-based than guideline-specific.
Provides clear, practical next steps for current transfer and contingency planning, including SET, hydrosalpinx review, luteal support, early pregnancy monitoring, and future-cycle considerations.
